words.sense: Extreme self-absorption and inflated self-importance that crowds out genuine concern for others.
words.connotation: strongly negative; in general use not a clinical diagnosis
misconceptions: Any interest in looking good proves narcissism.

words.sense: Excessive pride in appearance, achievements, or the opinion others hold of oneself.
misconceptions: Extreme disregard for other people is only harmless pride in appearance.

semantic_axes.description: Concern with appearance or achievement versus pervasive self-importance.
Self-regard that coexists with care versus self-absorption that displaces care.

edges.boundary_rule: Narcissism is extreme self-importance that eclipses concern for others, while vanity centers on pride in one’s looks or achievements.
clues_a: ignores others’ urgent needs to secure attention
assumes other people exist to serve them
takes credit while dismissing others’ contributions
irrelevant_clues: amount of money spent on clothes

misconceptions.M1: Any interest in looking good proves narcissism.
misconceptions.M2: Extreme disregard for other people is only harmless pride in appearance.
misconceptions.M3: A compliment or selfie alone is enough to assign either label.

chains.frame: Which word best describes Amara’s behavior after the award?

beats.text: Amara accepted the team award and told reporters she alone deserved every bit of credit.
beats.decisive_clue: claims sole credit while silencing teammates
beats.reason: Her sense of importance pushes other people aside.

beats.text: She cut off teammates who tried to mention their contributions.
beats.decisive_clue: dismisses teammates’ contributions to preserve her superiority
beats.reason: Silencing others shows extreme self-focus beyond simply enjoying recognition.

chains.feedback_short: Silencing others shows extreme self-focus beyond simply enjoying recognition.
chains.feedback_deep: Her sense of importance pushes other people aside. Silencing others shows extreme self-focus beyond simply enjoying recognition. Vanity wants to look exceptional; narcissism treats everyone else as secondary.
chains.contrast_rule: Vanity wants to look exceptional; narcissism treats everyone else as secondary.

hints.attention: What happens to other people’s contributions?
hints.axis: Concern with appearance or achievement versus pervasive self-importance.
hints.contrast: Vanity wants to look exceptional; narcissism treats everyone else as secondary.
